chunks: ʿĀṣim narrated from Muḥammad ibn Qays, from Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said: Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

Any man who leaves a surriyyah, whether she has a child, or there is a child in her womb, or she has no child, then if her master had freed her, she is freed. But if he did not free her until he died, then the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has already preceded regarding her, and the Book of Allah has greater right.

He said: If she has a child and he leaves wealth, she is placed in the share of her child, and the guardians of her child retain her until the child grows up. Then it is the child who frees her, if he wishes. They inherit her child so long as she remains a bondwoman. If her child frees her, she is freed. And if her child dies without having freed her, then if they wish they keep her enslaved, and if they wish they free her.

And Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام ruled regarding a man who left a bondwoman who had borne him a daughter, while she was young, except that she could express speech; then she freed her mother. The patrons of the father of the bondwoman disputed concerning it, so he validated her freeing of her mother.

key_terms.أَوْلِيَاءُ وَلَدِهَا: the guardians responsible for the child
key_terms.سُرِّيَّةً: a concubine or bondwoman owned by a man
key_terms.كِتَابُ اللَّهِ: the divine ruling established by Allah in revelation
key_terms.نَصِيبِ وَلَدِهَا: the inheritance share allotted to her child

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on a surriyyah or bondwoman who is left behind after her master dies and has borne him a child?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning a surriyyah left behind after her master's death, especially when she has borne him a child. It explains how her status relates to inheritance shares, the authority of the child or the child's guardians, and it records a judicial ruling of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام validating a daughter's emancipation of her mother.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.3513 - Asim narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays, who narrated from Abu Ja'far Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as), that Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, said:

"Any man who leaves behind a concubine (surriyah) who has a child, or is pregnant with a child, or has no child, then if her master had freed her, she is free. But if he did not free her before his death, then the Book of Allah (swt), the Almighty and Glorious, has already decided her case, and the Book of Allah (swt) is more deserving to be followed."

Imam (as) continued: "If she has a child and the man leaves wealth, then she is to be placed under the share of her child, and the guardians of the child shall keep her until the child grows up. At that point, the child has the right to free her if they wish.
Meanwhile, the guardians inherit the child's wealth as long as she remains a slave. If her child frees her, she becomes free. However, if her child dies without freeing her, the guardians have the option to either keep her as a slave or free her."

"Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, also ruled concerning a man who left behind a bondwoman who had borne him a daughter. The daughter was still young but capable of speaking. The daughter then freed her mother.
The guardians of the father's estate disputed this matter, but Commander of the Faithful, peace be upon him, upheld the daughter's act of freeing her mother."
